To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the postpartum period is a critical time in the development of obesity in the rat, 2) the lactation period is a critical period for reducing carcass fat, 3) pregnancy followed by lactation is a critical period in the development of carcass fat, and 4) the postwean recovery period is a critical phase in the development of increased carcass fat, even in food-restrained rats.
1) lactation reduces carcass fat content in rats, and 2) food restriction increases carcass fat content during the postweaning period.
1) lactation results in a significant decrease in carcass fat and 2) food restriction during lactation and recovery results in a significant increase in carcass protein and decrease in carcass lipid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of pregnancy and lactation on carcass composition.
the effects of reproduction and recovery from lactation on body composition.
the effects of pregnancy and lactation on the carcass composition of Osborne-Mendel female rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pregnancy, lactation, and the recovery period all have significant effects on carcass fat and water content.

pregnancy followed by no suckling and a recovery period of 21 days results in a net increase in carcass adiposity in ad libititum-fed rats and a greater increase in carcass weight in food-restricted animals.
lactation results in a reduction in carcass fat and that this reduction may be offset by the effects of pregnancy and food restriction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lactation is a catabolic process and pregnancy is an anabolic process, and that both processes are associated with increased carcass fat in the rat.
pregnancy, lactation, and the postweaning period are associated with significant changes in body composition.

lactation, in ad libitut-fed rats, is accompanied by a reduction in carcass fat and that the postweaning period is accompanied by an increase in carcasses fat in food-restricted and ad libitum fed rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pregnancy and lactation in rats are accompanied by significant alterations in carcass composition that are not fully reversed by the postweaning period.
pregnancy and lactation have different effects on the body composition of the mother.
the reproductive cycle is a major determinant of carcass composition in female rats.
